title: Mass spectrometry analysis of circulating breast cancer cells from a Xenograft mouse model
protocol: Gently centrifuge the CTC suspension at 72 × g for 4 min in a pre-cooled centrifuge to reduce the volume.
Gently resuspend the pellet in cold 1× DPBS and add the BSA-free antibody mix in a total volume of 500 μL.
Incubate for 30 min at RT and protect from light.
Wash the CTCs suspension using 1 mL of cold 1× DPBS.
Centrifuge at 72 × g for 4 min in a pre-cooled centrifuge.
Repeat the wash twice to ensure total elimination of excess antibodies.
Resuspend stained cells in 1–2 mL of cold 1× DPBS solution.
Transfer resuspended cells on ice.
Define the gating strategy to separate cells from debris and red blood cells based on their physical properties using SSC and FCS Width (W) and Length (L).
Separate single cells from clustered cells using both SSC and FCS W and L parameters.
Negatively gate single cells for CD45 expression while positively gating them for a chosen fluorophore, such as eYFP.
Repeat the gating process for clustered cells.
Sort a small quantity of cells into a plate or 1.5 mL tube to assess sample purity under a fluorescent microscope.
Check the purity of samples before starting each sort when sorting four populations simultaneously (Single CTCs eYFP (+), Single CTCs eYFP (-), Clusters eYFP (+), Clusters eYFP (-)).
Place 1.5 mL tubes in the collection casket with 0.5 mL of cold 1× DPBS.
Add DAPI to the sample at a ratio of 1:1000 immediately before starting the sort.
Start and monitor the sort process.
Collect a minimum of 10,000 events for single CTC samples.
For CTC clusters, collect based on the average cluster size calculated during a trial sort.
Gently centrifuge the CTC suspension at 72 × g for 4 min in a pre-cooled centrifuge to pellet the sorted CTCs.
Remove as much supernatant as possible.
Snap freeze the tubes containing the sorted samples in liquid nitrogen.
Store samples at −80°C for up to 1 month.
For longer storage (up to 3 months), store samples in liquid nitrogen.
Thaw sample tubes at room temperature.
Spin to re-pellet.
Add 50 μL of lysis buffer to cell pellets.
Sonicate samples using Bioruptor with settings of 30 seconds on, 30 seconds off for 10 cycles at 4°C.
Spin samples for 10 seconds at 2000 × g.
Heat samples at 300 rpm in a Thermomixer for 10 min at 95°C.
Insert the samples into the heating block with the lid open and close it after one minute.
Cool down samples at 25°C.
Spin down samples at 2000 × g for 10 s.
Add 1 μL of 0.75 M Chloroacetamide solution.
Incubate at 500 rpm in a Thermomixer for 30 min at 37°C.
Short spin samples at 2000 × g for 10 s.
Measure pH of the samples.
Adjust pH between 8 and 9 using 1M Ammonium bicarbonate if necessary.
Add trypsin to achieve a final enzyme/protein ratio of 1:50.
Digest samples for 12 h at 37°C.
Spin down samples at 2000 × g for 10 s the next day.
Add 50 μL of 5% TFA solution.
Check pH is less than 2; add additional 10 μL of 5% TFA if not reached.
A white precipitate should be visible after addition of TFA, dissolve with vortexing for 10 s using Wash 1 buffer.
Spin samples at 2000 × g for 10 seconds.
Place SDB-RPS cartridges in 2 mL flow-through collection tubes.
Add peptide samples to the cartridges and spin at 2’000 × g for 4 minutes at 25°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Increase speed by 200 × g and spin again if liquid does not pass completely.
Add 200 μL of Wash 1 buffer and spin down at 2’000 × g for 4 minutes at 25°C.
Repeat step of adding 200 μL of Wash 1 buffer and spinning until flow-through is discarded.
Add 200 μL of Wash 2 buffer and spin down at 2’000 × g for 4 minutes at 25°C.
Repeat previous washing process with Wash 2 buffer until flow-through is discarded.
Place cartridges in clean, labeled 2 mL tubes.
Add 100 μL of Elution buffer to elute peptides and spin at 2’000 × g for 2 minutes at 25°C.
Repeat step of adding Elution buffer and spinning until desired amount of peptide elution is achieved.
Dry eluted peptides in a vacuum concentrator at 50°C.
Reconstitute peptides in 20 μL of LC-MS buffer.
Add 20 μL of buffer to each sample.
Sonicate samples in Vial Tweeter sonicator (5 pulses, Amplitude 100%, cycle 0.5).
Shake samples at 1400 rpm in a Thermomixer for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Determine peptide concentration using a NanoDrop (wavelengths 280 - 340 nm).
Dilute samples with LC-MS buffer to a concentration of 0.25 ug/ul.
Transfer samples to the LC-MS vials.
Analyze by LC-MS using the gradient and instrument settings indicated in the materials and equipment section.
Inject up to 0.5 μg of peptide per run.
Store remaining peptides at −20°C for potential repeat analysis.
